This made me think of something that might be the case: The Taurus SE's take a different EGR valve than the other 98 trim models. (That was a real PITA when I had to buy one the first time) I wonder if that's the difference. I do not know if they use a different solenoid, but it is a possibility.

I'm not sure youa re going in the right direction here. The EGR solenoid receives battery power from harness splice #152 on the red wire, which also feeds the canister purge valve. THe PCM pulses ground on the brown/pink wire off and on very rapidly to modulate vacuum flow through the solenoid; it not a simple on or off deal. On a scope you can see this occurring; on a voltmeter you would likely only be seeing an average voltage being that the circuit is being pulsed on and off very rapidly. If you are determined to go in this direction with testing, unplug the solenoid, turn the key on, and measure from the red wire with one lead to battery negative with the other lead (NOT across the plug); you will likely see 12 volts. If not, unplug the canister puge at the same time and check again. If it is still not 12 volts, check the red wire in the purge connector for 12 volts. However, I think you are on the wrong track here.

FIrst, check the solenoid operation. Pull vacuum on one port with the syringe you used to test the valve; it should hold vacuum. Then, using jumper wires, connect the solenoid to battery + and -; it should open and not hold vacuum. If it works, then the solenoid is likely OK.

You should be able to make the engine idle very roughly, almost to the point of stalling, by manually opening the EGR valve. If you can not, or if idle only gets slightly rough, then there are likely blockages in the EGR passages; a very common point for carbon to accumulate is in the passages at the base of the throttle body.

THe P0401 stores when the PCM commands the EGR open, but DPFE voltage does not respond. If you can make the solenoid operate, and opening the EGR makes the engine idle extremely poorly indicating the passages are all open, then the problem is likely a frozen (faulty) DPFE sensor. THe original design DPFE sensors used on the Taruses were metal and had an extremely high failure rate; updated ones are black plastic. You might want to try replacing the DPFE sensor to see if it resolves the problem; if so, I very strongly recommend a genuine Ford (Motorcraft) one; we have run into many aftermarket ones, particularly from discount auto stores, that do not work to spec right out of the box causing the same code to store.

In my experience, about 95% of the time the code you ahve on that engine is caused by either a restricted EGR passage or a frozen DPFE sensor.

This kind of fault can be very difficult to accurately diagnose without the right test equipment. A professional scan tool has the ability to command the solenoid to actuate, and at the same time monitor DPFE response to see where the problem is occurring. If you can not figure it out easily, sometimes it is cheaper in the long run to pay a local tech to test the system for you before replacing any parts; usually it only takes a few minutes with the right tools and is pretty inexpensive.
